cases.name: prose_only
cases.why: Every fragment is a prose word; none survives. This is the defect NR-0003 §2.0 exists to fix.
cases.message: connection established to the downstream auckland region

cases.name: colon_prose
cases.why: A colon between two words is not evidence, and `received` is not key-like, so nothing is kept.

cases.name: colon_key_like
cases.why: After a colon the key must be key-like; an underscore and a digit both qualify, so both short values are kept.
cases.message: auth failed for access_token: shortval and for retry2: alsoshort

cases.name: colon_credential_word
cases.why: A bare credential word is key-like even with no underscore or digit.

cases.name: assignment
cases.why: `=` is evidence on its own, so both values are kept although neither has value shape.

cases.name: quoted_fragment
cases.why: Enclosing quotes keep a fragment that would otherwise be dropped as prose.

cases.name: trailing_punctuation
cases.why: The trailing comma is stripped; the fragment is unmistakable hex.

cases.name: unquoted_base64_padding_is_not_captured
cases.why: The padding is absent from the candidate, and not because it was stripped: `=` is not in the unquoted value's character class, so the match ends before it. `_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION` excluding `=` therefore only matters for a quoted fragment, which the next case covers.

cases.name: quoted_base64_padding_kept
cases.why: Inside quotes the fragment is `[^"]{8,}`, so the padding is captured, and it survives because `=` is deliberately not trailing punctuation.

cases.name: uuid_and_url
cases.why: Two unmistakable shapes with no key name; both are kept as slots.

cases.name: jwt_shape
cases.why: The JWT shape is unmistakable. Assembled from parts so the committed fixture does not contain a literal token-shaped string for a scanner to match.

cases.name: public_key_header
cases.why: The `-----BEGIN ` rule does **not** fire here: the space is not in the unquoted value class, so no candidate ever starts with it, and what survives is the base64 body instead. The rule is reachable for an attribute value and for a quoted fragment, which the next case covers. A public key, because a private-key header in a committed fixture is what gitleaks blocks.

cases.name: quoted_public_key_header
cases.why: Quoted, the fragment keeps its `-----BEGIN ` prefix, which is where the unmistakable rule applies.

cases.name: duplicate_value
cases.why: The same value twice yields one candidate.

cases.name: mixed_case_long_word
cases.why: A pure-letter fragment needs 20 characters and mixed case; the second is too short.

cases.name: digits_and_letters
cases.why: Eight or more characters with both a digit and a letter has value shape even with no key name.
